EMPIRICAL RESEARCH PLAN  
“Biological Innovation and the Development of American Agriculture, 1880-1930”

────────────────────────────────────────
1. Identification Strategy
────────────────────────────────────────
Primary strategy: Staggered Difference-in-Differences (DiD) with an event-study extension.

Why it fits  
• We observe the same geographic units (states) repeatedly over time and adoption dates vary widely.  
• Biological innovations (e.g., the first commercial release of a new corn or wheat variety) create a reasonably sharp “event.”  
• Long panel (≈10 census waves) lets us check pre-trends and dynamic treatment effects.  
• Recent econometric advances (Callaway-Sant’Anna 2021, Sun & Abraham 2020) address heterogeneous treatment timing, making estimates credible.

Complementary IV robustness: instrument adoption with distance to the nearest USDA experiment station in 1890 and the share of state legislative seats held by members of the Ag Appropriations Committee. This helps address remaining endogeneity of adoption.

────────────────────────────────────────
2. Treatment and Control
────────────────────────────────────────
Unit of analysis: state × crop × census year panel (≈48 × 5 × 11 ≈ 2,600 obs).

Treatment variable  
T_sct = 1 if, by year t, state s has ≥10 % of crop c acreage sown with the first scientifically bred variety released for that crop (e.g., “Reid’s Yellow Dent” corn). Once treated, always treated (absorbing).

Control group  
States (or crop-state pairs) that have not yet crossed the 10 % threshold in year t. They serve as “not-yet-treated” controls until their own adoption year; never-adopters remain pure controls.

Treatment timing  
First year a state-crop pair breaches 10 % improved-seed acreage based on census questions on “seed source or variety” (available 1900, 1910, 1920 etc.). We linearly interpolate for intercensal years.

Event time k = t − A_sc, where A_sc is the adoption year.

────────────────────────────────────────
3. Key Identifying Assumptions
────────────────────────────────────────
A1. Parallel trends: in the absence of biological innovations, treated and not-yet-treated state-crop pairs would have evolved similarly.  
Plausibility: agronomic conditions differ, but including state × crop fixed effects, soil quality, rainfall shocks, and crop-specific nationwide trends makes the assumption more credible.

A2. No anticipation: farmers do not significantly change behavior before new varieties become commercially available.  
Plausibility: most varieties diffused quickly after release; earlier experimentation was limited to test plots.

A3. Stable unit treatment value (no cross-state spillovers): adoption in one state does not immediately change yields in another (e.g., via seed trade).  
Plausibility: interstate seed markets existed, but freight costs and varietal adaptation constraints (e.g., growing-degree-days) limited spillovers; we will check robustness by excluding bordering states around early adopters.

A4. Adoption is the first-order driver of yield changes; no concurrent confounders perfectly aligned with adoption years.  
Plausibility: major mechanical innovations (tractor, combine) rolled out on a different timeline; we control for diffusion of tractors using Historical Census of Manufacturing data.

────────────────────────────────────────
4. Threats to Identification & Fixes
────────────────────────────────────────
T1. Differential pre-trends  
• Fix: event-study graph + F-tests that pre-treatment leads k ∈ {−6,…,−1} are jointly zero. Exclude adopters with significant pre-trends or interact state-level linear trends with pre-period.

T2. Omitted simultaneous technologies (e.g., fertilizer)  
• Fix: Add controls for synthetic-fertilizer tonnage per acre (from Fertilizer Association Yearbooks) and tractor density; include interaction of year FE with baseline mechanization quartiles.

T3. Endogenous adoption (high-productivity states adopt earlier)  
• Fix 1: Saturate specification with state × crop linear trends.  
• Fix 2: Two-stage-least-squares IV using distance to experiment station and political representation. First-stage F>10 check.

────────────────────────────────────────
5. R Code Outline
────────────────────────────────────────
```r
###############################################################
# 0. Packages
###############################################################
pacman::p_load(data.table, fixest, ggplot2, did, haven)

###############################################################
# 1. Load and merge data
###############################################################
ag    <- fread("census_agriculture.csv")          # yields, acreage
seed  <- fread("improved_seed_share.csv")         # % improved
soil  <- fread("soil_quality.csv")                # time-invariant
fert  <- fread("fertilizer_inputs.csv")           # tons per acre
tract <- fread("tractor_density.csv")             # tractors/acre
expst <- fread("distance_to_station.csv")         # IV 1
pol   <- fread("ag_committee_share.csv")          # IV 2

dt <- Reduce(function(x,y) merge(x,y, by=c("state","crop","year"),
                                 all=TRUE),
              list(ag, seed, soil, fert, tract, expst, pol))

###############################################################
# 2. Variable construction
###############################################################
dt[, treat := as.integer(seed_share >= .10)]   # ever-treated flag
dt[, adopt_year := ifelse(treat==1, min(year[treat==1]), NA),
    by = .(state, crop)]
dt[, g := ifelse(!is.na(adopt_year), adopt_year, 9999)]  # group
dt[, rel_year := year - adopt_year]                       # event time

# Outcome
dt[, log_yield := log(output_per_acre)]

###############################################################
# 3. Staggered DiD (Callaway-Sant’Anna)
###############################################################
att_gt <- att_gt(yname = "log_yield",
                 tname = "year",
                 idname = "id",            # create id = state*crop
                 gname = "g",
                 xformla = ~ soil_quality + fert_per_acre + tractor_density,
                 data = dt[year >= 1890 & year <= 1930])

agg_simple <- aggte(att_gt, type = "group")
summary(agg_simple)

# Event-study plot
es <- aggte(att_gt, type="dynamic")
ggplot(data = data.frame(es$egt, es$att.egt, es$se.egt),
       aes(x=es.egt, y=att.egt)) +
  geom_point() + geom_line() +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = att.egt - 1.96*se.egt,
                    ymax = att.egt + 1.96*se.egt)) +
  labs(x="Years since adoption", y="ATT on log yield")

###############################################################
# 4. 2SLS robustness
###############################################################
dt[, iv1 := distance_to_station]       # further = slower adoption
dt[, iv2 := ag_committee_share]

felm_iv <- feols(log_yield ~ treat | state^crop + year,
                 iv = ~ treat | iv1 + iv2, data = dt,
                 cluster = ~state)

summary(felm_iv)

###############################################################
# 5. Sensitivity: border-state drop
###############################################################
border_states <- fread("early_adopter_neighbors.csv")
dt_nospill <- dt[!state %in% border_states$state2]
feols(log_yield ~ treat | state^crop + year, data = dt_nospill,
      cluster = ~state) |> summary()
```

────────────────────────────────────────
6. Expected Results
────────────────────────────────────────
Economic theory: Improved seed increases land productivity mainly through higher yields and pest resistance.

Prior: +5 – 10 % increase in log(output/acre) within 5 years of adoption; effect should plateau thereafter.

────────────────────────────────────────
7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (DiD)
────────────────────────────────────────
C1 Parallel trends visually and statistically verified ............... 0.8  
C2 No anticipatory behavior .......................................... 0.7  
C3 No spillovers/SUTVA ............................................... 0.6  
C4 Correct timing & no misclassification ............................. 0.9  
C5 Appropriate inference / clustered SEs ............................. 1.0  

(Scale 1 = clearly satisfied; 0 = questionable. Average ≈ 0.8)

────────────────────────────────────────
The plan combines a modern staggered DiD framework with instrumental‐variable robustness to credibly isolate the causal contribution of biological innovation to U.S. agricultural productivity during a transformative era.
